newsitem.title: USA: Kyle is newest tropical storm in Caribbean.
newsitem.headline: Kyle is newest tropical storm in Caribbean.

text.p: Tropical Storm Kyle emerged in the western Caribbean on Friday and was expected to buffet Belize, the Yucatan Peninsula and Honduras with gusty winds and rain, the National Hurricane Center said.

Kyle had maximum sustained winds of 50 mph (80 kmh) and was located 80 miles (128 km) east-southeast of Belize City at 5 p.m. EDT (2100 GMT), hurricane forecasters said. The storm's exact position was at latitude 17.0 north and 87.2 west, and it was drifting west at 3 mph (5 kmh).

"We think it could get a little bit stronger before it moves over northern Central America and Mexico," said hurricane center forecaster Miles Lawrence. "It's moving so slowly that it may take another 24 hours before the center of the storm makes landfall."
Kyle grew out of stormy weather left behind by last week's Tropical Storm Josephine, which pushed through northern Florida and along the U.S. eastern seaboard.
"The circulation around Josephine is what pushed a lot of cold air southward, and that's the front which settled into the northwestern Caribbean and helped form Kyle," Lawrence said.
